data.name: ASM001_Next
data.value: Correct the code on this line, then build again.

data.name: ASM002_Next
data.value: Check this line: the program was built, but it may not do what you expect.

data.name: ASM003_Next
data.value: Read this together with the message before it.

data.name: BLD001_Next
data.value: Open Settings and set the path of nasm.exe, or reinstall Assembly Studio to restore the bundled NASM.

data.name: BLD002_What
data.value: NASM did not finish within {0} seconds, so the build was stopped.

data.name: BLD002_Next
data.value: Look for a %rep block or a macro that never ends, then build again.

data.name: BLD003_Next
data.value: Build again. If it keeps happening, check the NASM installation in Settings.

data.name: BLD004_What
data.value: NASM failed (exit code {0}) without reporting a source line. Its output is shown unchanged.

data.name: BLD004_Next
data.value: Read the NASM output. If it is empty, check the NASM installation in Settings.

data.name: BLD005_Next
data.value: Build again when you are ready.

data.name: BLD006_What
data.value: The program is {0:N0} bytes, but a .COM program can be at most 65,280 bytes (64 KiB minus the 256-byte PSP).

data.name: BLD006_Next
data.value: Make the program smaller. For example, reserve large buffers with resb in a section .bss, which takes no space in the file.

data.name: BLD007_What
data.value: This looks like MASM or TASM code ("{0}"). Assembly Studio uses NASM syntax.

data.name: BLD007_Next
data.value: Open Help ▸ NASM vs MASM to see how to write this in NASM syntax.

data.name: BLD008_Next
data.value: Use the bundled NASM 3.02 (clear the assembler path in Settings), or install NASM 3.02 or later.

data.name: BLD009_What
data.value: The CPU directive '{0}' is not supported. Assembly Studio targets the 8086 processor.

data.name: BLD009_Next
data.value: Remove the CPU directive or change it to 8086, then build again.
